clue.text: Don't utter the golden number — add some butter

parts.note: SH is the command to keep quiet
OR is gold in heraldry
ten is a number

explanation.surface: Someone is told to keep quiet about the golden number and to put a little butter in.
explanation.walkthrough: To shorten pastry is to work fat such as butter into it, which is why the fat is called shortening.
explanation.definitionFit: In baking, working fat into dough to make it crumbly is the cook's verb meaning to enrich with fat.

clue.text: A little music for 17?

parts.note: a little of the word music is its first three letters; in a down entry the answer's first word written upwards shows them

explanation.surface: A short piece of music, wondering if it suits a card game.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: written up the grid, SUM reads MUS, a little of 'music'. 17 down is ABRIDGE, which the phrase also means.
explanation.definitionFit: To summarise and to abridge both mean to condense into fewer words.

clue.text: Flower, gold one, at Number Two briefly

parts.note: OR is gold in heraldry
I is the Roman numeral for one
two's company, and company abbreviated is Co

explanation.surface: A golden person is found at the Number Two spot for a short time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is a crossword way of saying river, something that flows; the Orinoco is a South American river.
explanation.definitionFit: A flower in crosswords is anything that flows, such as a river like this one in Venezuela.

clue.text: Money for ring

definitions.meaning: a charge paid to use a road or bridge
to sound a bell slowly and repeatedly

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a fee for passage and the slow sounding of a bell.

clue.text: Note about a certain bum (male) madly uttered corrupt verse on faith 7-ed in Esther — blondes for heroes?

indicators.note: about means the note's letters go around the following pieces

parts.note: NB is nota bene, a written note
one as in a certain person
butt is American slang for the backside
he is a male pronoun
to rave is to speak madly, so raved

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled, so the letters are rearranged
in means placed inside the name

parts.note: the biblical queen's name, used as written

indicators.note: 7 down is curtail, so the word loses its tail

parts.note: taken as written before being cut short

explanation.surface: A rambling tale of someone raving bad verse about faith, ending by asking whether fair-haired women are for the brave.
explanation.walkthrough: '7-ed' means treated as 7 down, CURTAIL: here FAITH is cut short by two letters. The note NB wraps three pieces, and Esther is split so the cut-down word sits before its last letter. The line is from Dryden's Alexander's Feast.
explanation.definitionFit: Dryden's line says only the brave deserve the fair; fair here means beautiful women, so the blondes go to the heroes.

clue.text: Guides and indicts engineers

annotationWithheld.why: Guides and indicts engineers (7): the only parse reads 'indicts' as 'in DICTS', so the 'in' of indicts is both the insertion indicator and part of the word giving DICTS, one word doing two jobs

clue.text: See 4
People who applaud nonsense can be useful in the garden

definitions.text: can be useful in the garden

parts.note: rot is nonsense
people who give an ovation are jokingly called ovators

explanation.surface: Fans who clap rubbish are of some help with gardening.
explanation.walkthrough: OVATORS is an invented word for people who give ovations.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotovators are motorised tillers for breaking up soil, so they help a gardener.

clue.text: 1 across, the wagger and the wagged

parts.note: a cur, a mongrel dog, wags its tail
a tail is what a dog wags

explanation.surface: A dog and the thing it wags.
explanation.definitionFit: To curtail is to cut short, a synonym of the 1 across answer.

clue.text: Semi-slow cooker for East European

indicators.note: semi means half, so only the first half of the word is taken

parts.note: an oven is a cooker

explanation.surface: A half-speed stove for someone from Eastern Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A Slovene is a native of Slovenia, a country in Europe.

clue.text: Chief ways to be at home in Belgian city

indicators.note: the city surrounds the home word, so in signals placing one inside the other

parts.note: Malines is the French name of Mechelen in Belgium
at home means in

explanation.surface: A remark about the best routes to living in a particular Belgian town.
explanation.walkthrough: Malines is the French name for the Belgian city of Mechelen; IN goes after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Main lines are the principal railway routes, the chief tracks of a network.

clue.text: Trunk growing from roots

indicators.note: growing suggests development into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tree's trunk sprouting up from its roots.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk of the body, without head or limbs, is the anatomical term used here.

clue.text: Game of water polo?

parts.note: read as a game that is also a body of water, with the letters of polo jumbled as a hint, the question mark flagging the play

explanation.surface: A question about the sport played by swimmers with a ball.
explanation.walkthrough: One word is both a cue sport and a stretch of water, and water polo is played in one.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a billiards-type game and a body of water such as a swimming bath.

clue.text: Sailor accepting return of singular sort of word fed on 1 across

parts.note: AB is an able seaman

indicators.note: return means the following pieces are read backwards

parts.note: I is a single one, the Roman numeral for one
a verb is a kind of word
fed means ate

explanation.surface: A sailor takes in a backward word while dining on something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return of' turns I + VERB into BREVI. 1 across is SHORTEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To abbreviate is to cut short, a synonym of the 1 across answer.

clue.text: Medicine for St Giles's day — caper about

indicators.note: about means the caper's letters go around the date

parts.note: an antic is a playful caper
St Giles's feast day is 1 September, written Sept I

explanation.surface: A remedy prescribed for a saint's feast day, with some fun around it.
explanation.walkthrough: The feast of St Giles falls on 1 September, abbreviated SEPT I.
explanation.definitionFit: An antiseptic is a substance applied to prevent infection, a kind of medical treatment.

clue.text: 1 across topped otherwise by wasp

indicators.note: otherwise means arranged differently, so the remaining letters are rearranged
topped means having the top cut off, so the first letter goes

parts.note: the answer to 1 across

explanation.surface: A word with its top cut off is rearranged into an insect.
explanation.walkthrough: SHORTEN 'topped' loses S, leaving HORTEN, which 'otherwise' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The hornet is the largest European wasp, so it is an example of the insect.

clue.text: Pip's girl — is she from across the water?

definitions.meaning: in Dickens's Great Expectations, Pip loves the cold beauty raised by Miss Havisham

definitions.text: is she from across the water?
definitions.meaning: French ... means is she, and France lies across the Channel

explanation.surface: A question about whether Pip's sweetheart came from overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: Across the water means from France: French est elle is 'is she'.
explanation.definitionFit: Estella is the girl Pip loves in Great Expectations; the name is given in French form.

clue.text: 8 (say) is hot, conforming abjectly

parts.note: the 8 down answer, a person from Slovenia, is an example of a Slav
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

explanation.surface: Someone from Eastern Europe is warm and grovelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Slavish behaviour copies or obeys others without independence, like a slave.

clue.text: Get rid of qualification formerly in the wind

parts.note: to sack is to dismiss
but introduces a qualification, as in 'yes, but'

explanation.surface: Someone loses a qualification they once held in a blustery wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the wind' means in the wind section of a band: the sackbut was an early trombone.
explanation.definitionFit: The sackbut was a Renaissance brass instrument, an early wind instrument now superseded.

clue.text: A game 1 across

parts.note: bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A card game cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to cut it down, a synonym of the 1 across answer.

clue.text: 14's other seat

indicators.note: other signals a different arrangement of those letters

parts.note: the 14 across answer, the wasp

explanation.surface: The wasp has another place to sit.
explanation.walkthrough: The insect's letters rearranged make a seat; 'throne' is also slang for a lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: A throne is a ceremonial seat for a monarch, and jokingly a toilet seat.

clue.text: Not still angry? Toss coin about it

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the next piece
tossing jumbles something, so the letters of coin are rearranged

parts.note: mad means angry

explanation.surface: Someone restless and cross decides things by flipping a coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toss' rearranges COIN into NOIC, which goes 'about' MAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomadic people move from place to place, never staying still.

clue.text: Footsore cattle?

parts.note: cows with corns on their feet would be corned, a joke on the tinned meat

explanation.surface: Cows limping with sore feet.
explanation.walkthrough: Corned means salted, but read it as having corns on the feet.
explanation.definitionFit: The tinned salted meat is read jokingly as cattle with painful corns on their feet.

clue.text: In the course of finishing a wonderful building

indicators.note: finishing means taking only the end of the building's name, its opening letters removed

parts.note: the Great Pyramid was one of the Seven Wonders of the World

explanation.surface: Something happens while a marvellous building is being completed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pyramids of Giza were a Wonder of the World; the finishing part of PYRAMID is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Amid is a preposition meaning in the middle of or during.

clue.text: Spirit publicising the danger of spirits?

definitions.meaning: a wood nymph of Greek myth
read as an advertisement for abstaining from alcohol, an anti-drink advert

explanation.surface: A ghost warning about the hazards of strong drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into two words: DRY (no alcohol) and AD (advertisement).
explanation.definitionFit: A dryad is a tree nymph in Greek mythology, a nature spirit.

clue.text: Second child out of control?

parts.note: a kid is a child

explanation.surface: A second child who is running wild.
explanation.definitionFit: A skid is a sliding vehicle out of control, so the definition describes it loosely.

clue.text: Stay for a time in the bathroom

parts.note: to bide is to stay or wait
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone lingers a while in the bathroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A bidet is a low washing basin found as a bathroom fitting.

clue.text: A largely 1 across age — 24 hours, alas!

parts.note: most of the 1 across answer is short, and short plus age gives shortage, a lack
24 hours is a day, so a day

explanation.surface: Lamenting an era cut short in a single day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely 1 across' is SHORT (SHORTEN without its last two letters), and with 'age' it makes SHORTAGE, which is LACK.
explanation.definitionFit: Alackaday is an archaic exclamation of sorrow, an old synonym for alas.

clue.text: The Dormouse's well content

parts.note: in Alice in Wonderland the Dormouse tells of three sisters living at the bottom of a well filled with a sweet syrup

explanation.surface: A sleepy little animal is quite happy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well content' looks like 'quite happy', but it is what fills the well in the Dormouse's story at the Mad Hatter's tea party.
explanation.definitionFit: In Lewis Carroll's tale the Dormouse's well is filled with sweet golden syrup.

clue.text: Communist holds Fascist leader 1across-ed

indicators.note: holds means one piece contains the other

parts.note: red is a common word for a communist
Il Duce was the title of Mussolini, the Italian Fascist leader

explanation.surface: A communist grips a fascist chief, cutting him down to size.
explanation.walkthrough: '1across-ed' means shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: Reduced means made smaller or cut down, a synonym of shortened.
